<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial><STRONG>Mid-Cap Growth Index Fund</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=Arial><STRONG>Notes to Financial Statements</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Vanguard Mid-Cap Growth Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers three classes of shares: Investor Shares, ETF Shares, and Admiral Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#8217;s minimum purchase requirements. ETF Shares are listed for trading on NYSE Arca; they can be purchased and sold through a broker. Admiral Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, service, and account-size criteria.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>A. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. investment companies. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4 p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#8217;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#8217; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#8217;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market. Counterparty risk involving futures is mitigated because a regulated clearinghouse is the counterparty instead of the clearing broker. To further mitigate counterparty risk, the fund trades futures contracts on an exchange, monitors the financial strength of its clearing brokers and clearinghouse, and has entered into clearing agreements with its clearing brokers. The clearinghouse imposes initial margin requirements to secure the fund&#8217;s performance and requires daily settlement of variation margin representing changes in the market value of each contract.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate settlement values of the contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>During the year ended December 31, 2016, the fund&#8217;s average investments in long and short futures contracts represented less than 1% and 0% of net assets, respectively, based on the average of aggregate settlement values at each quarter-end during the period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>69</FONT></P></DIV>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial><STRONG>Mid-Cap Growth Index Fund</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>3. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Management has analyzed the fund&#8217;s tax positions taken for all open federal income tax years (December 31, 2013&#8211;2016), and has concluded that no provision for federal income tax is required in the fund&#8217;s financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>4. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>5. Securities Lending: To earn additional income, the fund lends its securities to qualified institutional borrowers. Security loans are subject to termination by the fund at any time, and are required to be secured at all times by collateral in an amount at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. Daily market fluctuations could cause the value of loaned securities to be more or less than the value of the collateral received. When this occurs, the collateral is adjusted and settled on the next business day. The fund further mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into securities lending transactions only with a diverse group of prequalified counterparties, monitoring their financial strength, and entering into master securities lending agreements with its counterparties. The master securities lending agreements provide that, in the event of a counterparty&#8217;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may terminate any loans with that borrower, determine the net amount owed, and sell or retain the collateral up to the net amount owed to the fund; however, such actions may be subject to legal proceedings. While collateral mitigates counterparty risk, in the absence of a default the fund may experience delays and costs in recovering the securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability in the Statement of Net Assets for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Securities lending income represents fees charged to borrowers plus income earned on invested cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan. During the term of the loan, the fund is entitled to all distributions made on or in respect of the loaned securities.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>6. Credit Facility: The fund and certain other funds managed by The Vanguard Group (&#8220;Vanguard&#8221;) participate in a $3.1 billion committed credit facility provided by a syndicate of lenders pursuant to a credit agreement that may be renewed annually; each fund is individually liable for its borrowings, if any, under the credit facility. Borrowings may be utilized for temporary and emergency purposes, and are subject to the fund&#8217;s regulatory and contractual borrowing restrictions. The participating funds are charged administrative fees and an annual commitment fee of 0.10% of the undrawn amount of the facility; these fees are allocated to the funds based on a method approved by the fund&#8217;s board of trustees and included in Management and Administrative expenses on the fund&#8217;s Statement of Operations. Any borrowings under this facility bear interest at a rate based upon the higher of the one-month London Interbank Offered Rate, federal funds effective rate, or overnight bank funding rate plus an agreed-upon spread.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The fund had no borrowings outstanding at December 31, 2016, or at any time during the period then ended.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>7. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Premiums and discounts on debt securities purchased are amortized and accreted, respectively, to interest income over the lives of the respective securities. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial><STRONG>Mid-Cap Value Index Fund</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=Arial><STRONG>Notes to Financial Statements</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Vanguard Mid-Cap Value Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers three classes of shares: Investor Shares, ETF Shares and Admiral Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#8217;s minimum purchase requirements. ETF Shares are listed for trading on NYSE Arca; they can be purchased and sold through a broker. Admiral Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, service, and account-size criteria.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>A. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. investment companies. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4 p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#8217;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#8217; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#8217;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market. Counterparty risk involving futures is mitigated because a regulated clearinghouse is the counterparty instead of the clearing broker. To further mitigate counterparty risk, the fund trades futures contracts on an exchange, monitors the financial strength of its clearing brokers and clearinghouse, and has entered into clearing agreements with its clearing brokers. The clearinghouse imposes initial margin requirements to secure the fund&#8217;s performance and requires daily settlement of variation margin representing changes in the market value of each contract.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate settlement values of the contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>During the year ended December 31, 2016, the fund&#8217;s average investments in long and short futures contracts represented less than 1% and 0% of net assets, respectively, based on the average of aggregate settlement values at each quarter-end during the period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>86</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<!--$$/page=--><A name="page_214"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder214"></a><DIV style="PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial><STRONG>Mid-Cap Value Index Fund</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>3. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Management has analyzed the fund&#8217;s tax positions taken for all open federal income tax years (December 31, 2013&#8211;2016), and has concluded that no provision for federal income tax is required in the fund&#8217;s financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>4. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>5. Securities Lending: To earn additional income, the fund lends its securities to qualified institutional borrowers. Security loans are subject to termination by the fund at any time, and are required to be secured at all times by collateral in an amount at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. Daily market fluctuations could cause the value of loaned securities to be more or less than the value of the collateral received. When this occurs, the collateral is adjusted and settled on the next business day. The fund further mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into securities lending transactions only with a diverse group of prequalified counterparties, monitoring their financial strength, and entering into master securities lending agreements with its counterparties. The master securities lending agreements provide that, in the event of a counterparty&#8217;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may terminate any loans with that borrower, determine the net amount owed, and sell or retain the collateral up to the net amount owed to the fund; however, such actions may be subject to legal proceedings. While collateral mitigates counterparty risk, in the absence of a default the fund may experience delays and costs in recovering the securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability in the Statement of Net Assets for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Securities lending income represents fees charged to borrowers plus income earned on invested cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan. During the term of the loan, the fund is entitled to all distributions made on or in respect of the loaned securities.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>6. Credit Facility: The fund and certain other funds managed by The Vanguard Group (&#8220;Vanguard&#8221;) participate in a $3.1 billion committed credit facility provided by a syndicate of lenders pursuant to a credit agreement that may be renewed annually; each fund is individually liable for its borrowings, if any, under the credit facility. Borrowings may be utilized for temporary and emergency purposes, and are subject to the fund&#8217;s regulatory and contractual borrowing restrictions. The participating funds are charged administrative fees and an annual commitment fee of 0.10% of the undrawn amount of the facility; these fees are allocated to the funds based on a method approved by the fund&#8217;s board of trustees and included in Management and Administrative expenses on the fund&#8217;s Statement of Operations. Any borrowings under this facility bear interest at a rate based upon the higher of the one-month London Interbank Offered Rate, federal funds effective rate, or overnight bank funding rate plus an agreed-upon spread.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The fund had no borrowings outstanding at December 31, 2016, or at any time during the period then ended.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>7. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Premiums and discounts on debt securities purchased are amortized and accreted, respectively, to interest income over the lives of the respective securities. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>87</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<!--$$/page=--><A name="page_215"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder215"></a><DIV style="PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial><STRONG>Mid-Cap Value Index Fund</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Each class of shares has equal rights as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately bears certain class-specific expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in Management and Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses are allocated to each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees. Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>B. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>In accordance with the terms of a Funds&#8217; Service Agreement (the &#8220;FSA&#8221;) between Vanguard and the fund, Vanguard furnishes to the fund investment advisory, corporate management, administrative, marketing, and distribution services at Vanguard&#8217;s cost of operations (as defined by the FSA). These costs of operations are allocated to the fund based on methods and guidelines approved by the board of trustees. Vanguard does not require reimbursement in the current period for certain costs of operations (such as deferred compensation/benefits and risk/insurance costs); the fund&#8217;s liability for these costs of operations is included in Payables to Vanguard on the Statement of Net Assets.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Upon the request of Vanguard, the fund may invest up to 0.40% of its net assets as capital in Vanguard. At December 31, 2016, the fund had contributed to Vanguard capital in the amount of $939,000, representing 0.01% of the fund&#8217;s net assets and 0.38% of Vanguard&#8217;s capitalization. The fund&#8217;s trustees and officers are also directors and employees, respectively, of Vanguard.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>C. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Various inputs may be used to determine the value of the fund&#8217;s investments. These inputs are summarized in three broad levels for financial statement purposes. The inputs or methodologies used to value securities are not necessarily an indication of the risk associated with investing in those securities.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial><STRONG>Level 1</STRONG></FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial><STRONG>&#8212;</STRONG>Quoted prices in active markets for identical securities.</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial><STRONG>Level 2</STRONG></FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial><STRONG>&#8212;</STRONG>Other significant observable inputs (including quoted prices for similar securities, interest </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>rates, prepayment speeds, credit risk, etc.).</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial><STRONG>Level 3</STRONG></FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial><STRONG>&#8212;</STRONG>Significant unobservable inputs (including the fund&#8217;s own assumptions used to determine </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>the fair value of investments).</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Unrealized appreciation (depreciation) on open futures contracts is required to be treated as realized gain (loss) for tax purposes.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>E. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character. Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes. These differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as ordinary income for tax purposes.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>During the year ended December 31, 2016, the fund realized $578,156,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind redemptions&#8212;in which shareholders exchanged fund shares for securities held by the fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized losses to paid-in capital.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>For tax purposes, at December 31, 2016, the fund had $1,714,000 of ordinary income available for distribution. At December 31, 2016, the fund had available capital losses totaling $497,430,000 to offset future net capital gains. Of this amount, $4,037,000 is subject to expiration on December 31, 2018. Capital losses of $493,393,000 realized beginning in fiscal 2012 may be carried forward indefinitely under the Regulated Investment Company Modernization Act of 2010, but must be used before any expiring loss carryforwards.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>At December 31, 2016, the cost of investment securities for tax purposes was $11,339,469,000. Net unrealized appreciation of investment securities for tax purposes was $1,703,073,000, consisting of unrealized gains of $2,002,207,000 on securities that had risen in value since their purchase and $299,134,000 in unrealized losses on securities that had fallen in value since their purchase.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>F. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>During the year ended December 31, 2016, the fund purchased $6,520,750,000 of investment securities and sold $3,668,757,000 of investment securities, other than temporary cash investments. Purchases and sales include $2,609,330,000 and $1,527,892,000, respectively, in connection with in-kind purchases and redemptions of the fund&#8217;s capital shares.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The fund purchased securities from and sold securities to other Vanguard funds or accounts managed by Vanguard or its affiliates, in accordance with procedures adopted by the board of trustees in compliance with Rule 17a-7 of the Investment Company Act of 1940. <P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=Arial><STRONG>Your Fund&#8217;s After-Tax Returns</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>This table presents returns for your fund both before and after taxes. The after-tax returns are shown in two ways: (1) assuming that an investor owned the fund during the entire period and paid taxes on the fund&#8217;s distributions, and (2) assuming that an investor paid taxes on the fund&#8217;s distributions </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>and </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>sold all shares at the end of each period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Calculations are based on the highest individual federal income tax and capital gains tax rates in effect at the times of the distributions and the hypothetical sales. State and local taxes were not considered. After-tax returns reflect any qualified dividend income. (In the example, returns after the sale of fund shares may be higher than those assuming no sale. This occurs when the sale would have produced a capital loss. The calculation assumes that the investor received a tax deduction for the loss.)</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The table shows returns for Investor Shares only; returns for other share classes will differ. Please note that your actual after-tax returns will depend on your tax situation and may differ from those shown. Also note that if you own the fund in a tax-deferred account, such as an individual retirement account or a 401(k) plan, this information does not apply to you. Such accounts are not subject to current taxes.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Finally, keep in mind that a fund&#8217;s performance&#8212;whether before or after taxes&#8212;does not guarantee future results.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=Arial><STRONG>About Your Fund&#8217;s Expenses</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>As a shareholder of the fund, you incur ongoing costs, which include costs for portfolio management, administrative services, and shareholder reports (like this one), among others. Operating expenses, which are deducted from a fund&#8217;s gross income, directly reduce the investment return of the fund.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>A fund&#8217;s expenses are expressed as a percentage of its average net assets. This figure is known as the expense ratio. The following examples are intended to help you understand the ongoing costs (in dollars) of investing in your fund and to compare these costs with those of other mutual funds. The examples are based on an investment of $1,000 made at the beginning of the period shown and held for the entire period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The accompanying table illustrates your fund&#8217;s costs in two ways:</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>&#8226; </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Based on actual fund return. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>This section helps you to estimate the actual expenses that you paid over the period. The &#8221;Ending Account Value&#8220; shown is derived from the fund&#8216;s actual return, and the third column shows the dollar amount that would have been paid by an investor who started with $1,000 in the fund. You may use the information here, together with the amount you invested, to estimate the expenses that you paid over the period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>To do so, simply divide your account value by $1,000 (for example, an $8,600 account value divided by $1,000 = 8.6), then multiply the result by the number given for your fund under the heading &#8221;Expenses Paid During Period.&#8220;</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>&#8226; </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Based on hypothetical 5% yearly return. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>This section is intended to help you compare your fund&#8216;s costs with those of other mutual funds. It assumes that the fund had a yearly return of 5% before expenses, but that the expense ratio is unchanged. In this case&#8212;because the return used is not the fund&#8217;s actual return&#8212;the results do not apply to your investment. The example is useful in making comparisons because the Securities and Exchange Commission requires all mutual funds to calculate expenses based on a 5% return. You can assess your fund&#8217;s costs by comparing this hypothetical example with the hypothetical examples that appear in shareholder reports of other funds.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Note that the expenses shown in the table are meant to highlight and help you compare </FONT><I><FONT size=1 face=Arial>ongoing </FONT></I><FONT size=1 face=Arial>costs only and do not reflect transaction costs incurred by the fund for buying and selling securities. Further, the expenses do not include any purchase, redemption, or account service fees described in the fund prospectus. If such fees were applied to your account, your costs would be higher. Your fund does not carry a &#8220;sales load.&#8221;</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The calculations assume no shares were bought or sold during the period. Your actual costs may have been higher or lower, depending on the amount of your investment and the timing of any purchases or redemptions.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>You can find more information about the fund&#8217;s expenses, including annual expense ratios, in the Financial Statements section of this report. For additional information on operating expenses and other shareholder costs, please refer to your fund&#8217;s current prospectus.</FONT></P>

<a name="_bclPageBorder225"></a><DIV style="PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=Arial><STRONG>Glossary</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>30-Day SEC Yield. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>A fund&#8217;s 30-day SEC yield is derived using a formula specified by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. Under the formula, data related to the fund&#8217;s security holdings in the previous 30 days are used to calculate the fund&#8217;s hypothetical net income for that period, which is then annualized and divided by the fund&#8217;s estimated average net assets over the calculation period. For the purposes of this calculation, a security&#8217;s income is based on its current market yield to maturity (for bonds), its actual income (for asset-backed securities), or its projected dividend yield (for stocks). Because the SEC yield represents hypothetical annualized income, it will differ&#8212;at times significantly&#8212;from the fund&#8217;s actual experience. As a result, the fund&#8217;s income distributions may be higher or lower than implied by the SEC yield.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Beta. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>A measure of the magnitude of a fund&#8217;s past share-price fluctuations in relation to the ups and downs of a given market index. The index is assigned a beta of 1.00. Compared with a given index, a fund with a beta of 1.20 typically would have seen its share price rise or fall by 12% when the index rose or fell by 10%. For this report, beta is based on returns over the past 36 months for both the fund and the index. Note that a fund&#8217;s beta should be reviewed in conjunction with its R-squared (see definition). The lower the R-squared, the less correlation there is between the fund and the index, and the less reliable beta is as an indicator of volatility.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Dividend Yield. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Dividend income earned by stocks, expressed as a percentage of the aggregate market value (or of net asset value, for a fund). The yield is determined by dividing the amount of the annual dividends by the aggregate value (or net asset value) at the end of the period. For a fund, the dividend yield is based solely on stock holdings and does not include any income produced by other investments.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Earnings Growth Rate. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The average annual rate of growth in earnings over the past five years for the stocks now in a fund.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Equity Exposure. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>A measure that reflects a fund&#8217;s investments in stocks and stock futures. Any holdings in short-term reserves are excluded.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Expense Ratio. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>A fund&#8217;s total annual operating expenses expressed as a percentage of the fund&#8217;s average net assets. The expense ratio includes management and administrative expenses, but does not include the transaction costs of buying and selling portfolio securities.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Foreign Holdings. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The percentage of a fund represented by securities or depositary receipts of companies based outside the United States.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Inception Date. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The date on which the assets of a fund (or one of its share classes) are first invested in accordance with the fund&#8217;s investment objective. For funds with a subscription period, the inception date is the day after that period ends. Investment performance is measured from the inception date.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Median Market Cap. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>An indicator of the size of companies in which a fund invests; the midpoint of market capitalization (market price x shares outstanding) of a fund&#8217;s stocks, weighted by the proportion of the fund&#8217;s assets invested in each stock. Stocks representing half of the fund&#8217;s assets have market capitalizations above the median, and the rest are below it.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Price/Book Ratio. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The share price of a stock divided by its net worth, or book value, per share. For a fund, the weighted average price/book ratio of the stocks it holds.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>98</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<!--$$/page=--><A name="page_226"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder226"></a><DIV style="PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Price/Earnings Ratio. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The ratio of a stock&#8217;s current price to its per-share earnings over the past year. For a fund, the weighted average P/E of the stocks it holds. P/E is an indicator of market expectations about corporate prospects; the higher the P/E, the greater the expectations for a company&#8217;s future growth.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>R-Squared. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>A measure of how much of a fund&#8217;s past returns can be explained by the returns from the market in general, as measured by a given index. If a fund&#8217;s total returns were precisely synchronized with an index&#8217;s returns, its R-squared would be 1.00. If the fund&#8217;s returns bore no relationship to the index&#8217;s returns, its R-squared would be 0. For this report, R-squared is based on returns over the past 36 months for both the fund and the index.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Return on Equity. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The annual average rate of return generated by a company during the past five years for each dollar of shareholder&#8217;s equity (net income divided by shareholder&#8217;s equity). For a fund, the weighted average return on equity for the companies whose stocks it holds.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Short-Term Reserves. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The percentage of a fund invested in highly liquid, short-term securities that can be readily converted to cash.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Turnover Rate. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>An indication of the fund&#8217;s trading activity. Funds with high turnover rates incur higher transaction costs and may be more likely to distribute capital gains (which may be taxable to investors). The turnover rate excludes in-kind transactions, which have minimal impact on costs.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>Benchmark Information</FONT><BR><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Spliced Mid-Cap Growth Index: </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>MSCI US Mid Cap Growth Index through April 16, 2013; CRSP US</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Mid Cap Growth Index thereafter.</FONT><BR><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Spliced Mid-Cap Index: </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>S&amp;P MidCap 400 Index through May 16, 2003;&nbsp;MSCI US Mid Cap 450</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Index through January 30, 2013;&nbsp;CRSP US Mid Cap Index thereafter.</FONT><BR><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Spliced Mid-Cap Value Index: </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>MSCI US Mid Cap Value Index through April 16, 2013; CRSP US Mid</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Cap Value Index thereafter.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>99</FONT></P></DIV>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial><STRONG>A new format, unwavering commitment</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>As you begin reading this report, you&#8217;ll notice that we&#8217;ve made some improvements to the opening sections&#8212;based on feedback from you, our clients.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>Page 1 starts with a new &#8221;Your Fund&#8217;s Performance at a Glance,&#8221; a concise, handy summary of how your fund performed during the period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>In the renamed &#8221;Chairman&#8217;s Perspective,&#8221; Bill McNabb will focus on enduring principles and investment insights.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>We&#8217;ve modified some tables, and eliminated some redundancy, but we haven&#8217;t removed any information.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>At Vanguard, we&#8217;re always looking for better ways to communicate and to help you make sound investment decisions. Thank you for entrusting your assets to us.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=Arial><STRONG>Your Fund&#8217;s Performance at a Glance</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>&#8226; Returns ranged from nearly 17% for Vanguard Value Index Fund to about 6% for Vanguard Growth Index Fund. Vanguard Large-Cap Index Fund, which contains both growth and value stocks, returned more than 11%.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>&#8226; All three funds closely tracked their target indexes and surpassed the average returns of their peers.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>&#8226; Small-capitalization stocks outperformed their large- and mid-cap counterparts, and value stocks outpaced growth.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>&#8226; Financial stocks were the top contributors for the Large-Cap Index Fund and the Value Index Fund. Technology stocks added most to the Growth Index Fund. Oil and gas and industrial holdings were among the best performers for all three funds. The health care sector produced negative results for the Growth Index Fund and the Large-Cap Index Fund.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>&#8226; Over the past decade, all three funds posted returns in line with their benchmark indexes and ahead of the average return of their peers.</FONT></P>

<a name="_bclPageBorder239"></a><DIV style="PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=Arial><STRONG>Chairman&#8217;s Perspective</STRONG></FONT></P>
<IMG border=0 src="usstockindexfunds_larg-cx6x1.jpg"> <BR>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Bill McNabb</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Chairman and Chief Executive Officer</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>Dear Shareholder,</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial><STRONG>If you&#8217;re like most investors, a big question on your mind is: What&#8217;s in store for the markets and the economy in 2017?</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>At Vanguard, we&#8217;re just as curious about the immediate future. But our curiosity is tempered by our belief that forecasts should give a range of possible outcomes, not pinpoint predictions. After all, there are bound to be occurrences the experts won&#8217;t see coming.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial><STRONG>What really matters for investors</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>In 2016, we saw two cases in point: The United Kingdom&#8217;s June vote to exit the European Union and the November election of Donald Trump as U.S. president. Both unexpected outcomes triggered swift market reactions. But despite some short-term volatility, the markets&#8217; 12-month performance as of December 31, 2016, proved to be less dramatic. U.S. stocks posted healthy returns, and U.S. bonds provided returns close to their long-term averages. International stocks and bonds also advanced, although returns for U.S. investors were reduced by the strength of the U.S. dollar.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>The surprises of 2016 remind us to be skeptical of overly precise short-term predictions about 2017. At the cusp of a new year, market prognosticators forecast where the Standard &amp; Poor&#8217;s 500 Index or the yield on the 10-year Treasury note will end up in 12 months. Such predictions can be attention-getting. They can also be dead wrong.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>4</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<!--$$/page=--><A name="page_240"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder240"></a><DIV style="PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>Investors are better off taking note of long-term trends that stand to influence our economies and markets. We&#8217;re watching these trends closely, and we discuss our latest assessment in our 2017 economic and market outlook, which you can read at vanguard.com/research.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial><STRONG>Our global economic outlook: Expect stabilization, not stagnation</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>One phenomenon in particular that we&#8217;re watching is the low-growth, low-interest-rate environment that has marked the global economy since the 2008&#8211;09 financial crisis. We don&#8217;t think this economic backdrop is simply the result of cyclically weak demand or long-term stagnation. Instead, certain structural forces are contributing: Falling technology costs are restraining the amounts businesses are spending on </FONT><FONT size=2 face=Arial>capital investment, an aging population is weighing on growth in the developed world, and the free movement of capital and products across the globe has restrained prices and wages.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>In the near term, these forces will continue to dampen growth, inflation, and interest rates. They also make it unlikely that further monetary stimulus from central banks will do much to spur growth.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>I realize this all may sound gloomy, but that&#8217;s not how we see it. We expect global growth to stabilize at more modest levels, not stagnate. The world isn&#8217;t headed for Japanese-style deflation, in which a widespread sustained drop in prices puts economic activity into hibernation.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>5</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<a name="_bclPageBorder241"></a><DIV style="PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>In fact, we believe that global growth could pick up modestly over time. Our expectation is based on a potential rebound in productivity as new digital technologies are used more effectively. We also anticipate a slight recovery in the labor force as the baby boom generation finishes its transition to retirement, nudging up demand for workers.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial><STRONG>Put expansion in perspective</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>Looking to the United States, the world&#8217;s largest economy remains firmly on a long-term-growth path of about 2% per year. That&#8217;s lower than the historical average of 3.25% since 1950. We see such growth at this level as fundamentally sound, rather than abnormally low. Our evaluation takes into account lower U.S. population growth </FONT><FONT size=2 face=Arial>and the reality that the economic expansion from the 1980s until the financial crisis was fueled by debt, distorting the numbers.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>Turning to prices, we think that core U.S. inflation should modestly exceed 2% in 2017. That, in turn, will support further interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve, similar to the one at the end of 2016.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>We expect the Fed to raise rates in 2017 before taking an extended pause, and we see the federal funds rate staying below 2% through at least 2018.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial><STRONG>Prepare for muted returns</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>And what about prospects for the markets? Vanguard&#8217;s outlook for global stocks and bonds remains the most guarded in ten years, given fairly high stock valuations</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>and the low-interest-rate environment. We don&#8217;t expect global bond yields to increase materially from year-end 2016 levels.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>Our outlook for global equities is annualized returns of 5%&#8211;8% over the next decade. This outlook isn&#8217;t bearish, but is actually fairly positive when you take into account the current low-rate environment. (See the box titled </FONT><FONT size=2 face=Arial>Expect more modest returns, rely on time-tested principles </FONT><FONT size=2 face=Arial>for more.)</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial><STRONG>Focus on the four keys to investment success</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>Significant trends often happen gradually. Like shifting tides, they&#8217;re sometimes barely noticeable at first but ultimately can change the landscape entirely. Other times, apparent trends can end up receding before they have much of a long-term impact. Given the future&#8217;s inherent unpredictability, it&#8217;s not reasonable to expect a surefire block-buster revelation from any prognosticator or investment firm.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>What to conclude, then? No matter what scenario plays out, we believe investors have the best chance for success if they stay focused on what they can control: their goals, asset allocation, and investment costs, along with the discipline to stick to a plan. As Tim Buckley, our chief investment officer, likes to say, this can be easy to say but harder to do, especially in times of uncertainty. Investors who can stay focused on those four keys will find themselves well-positioned to weather any market.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Arial>As always, thank you for investing with Vanguard.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>IMPORTANT: The projections and other information generated by the Vanguard Capital Markets Model regarding</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>the likelihood of various investment outcomes are hypothetical in nature, do not reflect actual investment results,</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>and are not guarantees of future results. VCMM results will vary with each use and over time.</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The VCMM projections are based on a statistical analysis of historical data. Future returns may behave differently from the</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>historical patterns captured in the VCMM. More important, the VCMM may be underestimating extreme negative scenarios</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>unobserved in the historical period on which the model estimation is based.</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The VCMM is a proprietary financial simulation tool developed and maintained by Vanguard&#8217;s Investment Strategy Group.</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The model forecasts distributions of future returns for a wide array of broad asset classes. Those asset classes include U.S.</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>and international equity markets, several maturities of the U.S. Treasury and corporate fixed income markets, international</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>fixed income markets, U.S. money markets, commodities, and certain alternative investment strategies. The theoretical and</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>empirical foundation for the Vanguard Capital Markets Model is that the returns of various asset classes reflect the compensation</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>investors require for bearing different types of systematic risk (beta). At the core of the model are estimates of the dynamic</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>statistical relationship between risk factors and asset returns, obtained from statistical analysis based on available monthly</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>financial and economic data. Using a system of estimated equations, the model then applies a Monte Carlo simulation method</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>to project the estimated interrelationships among risk factors and asset classes as well as uncertainty and randomness over</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>time. The model generates a large set of simulated outcomes for each asset class over several time horizons. Forecasts are</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>obtained by computing measures of central tendency in these simulations. Results produced by the tool will vary with each</FONT><BR><FONT size=1 face=Arial>use and over time.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial><STRONG>Growth Index Fund</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=Arial><STRONG>Notes to Financial Statements</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Vanguard Growth Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers four classes of shares: Investor Shares, ETF Shares, Admiral Shares, and Institutional Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#8217;s minimum purchase requirements. ETF Shares are listed for trading on NYSE Arca; they can be purchased and sold through a broker. Admiral Shares and Institutional Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, service, and account-size criteria.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>A. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. investment companies. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4 p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#8217;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#8217; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#8217;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market. Counterparty risk involving futures is mitigated because a regulated clearinghouse is the counterparty instead of the clearing broker. To further mitigate counterparty risk, the fund trades futures contracts on an exchange, monitors the financial strength of its clearing brokers and clearinghouse, and has entered into clearing agreements with its clearing brokers. The clearinghouse imposes initial margin requirements to secure the fund&#8217;s performance and requires daily settlement of variation margin representing changes in the market value of each contract.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate settlement values of the contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>During the year ended December 31, 2016, the fund&#8217;s average investments in long and short futures contracts represented less than 1% and 0% of net assets, respectively, based on the average of aggregate settlement values at each quarter-end during the period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>24</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<!--$$/page=--><A name="page_260"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder260"></a><DIV style="PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial><STRONG>Growth Index Fund</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>3. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Management has analyzed the fund&#8217;s tax positions taken for all open federal income tax years (December 31, 2013&#8211;2016), and has concluded that no provision for federal income tax is required in the fund&#8217;s financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>4. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>5. Securities Lending: To earn additional income, the fund lends its securities to qualified institutional borrowers. Security loans are subject to termination by the fund at any time, and are required to be secured at all times by collateral in an amount at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. Daily market fluctuations could cause the value of loaned securities to be more or less than the value of the collateral received. When this occurs, the collateral is adjusted and settled on the next business day. The fund further mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into securities lending transactions only with a diverse group of prequalified counterparties, monitoring their financial strength, and entering into master securities lending agreements with its counterparties. The master securities lending agreements provide that, in the event of a counterparty&#8217;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may terminate any loans with that borrower, determine the net amount owed, and sell or retain the collateral up to the net amount owed to the fund; however, such actions may be subject to legal proceedings. While collateral mitigates counterparty risk, in the absence of a default the fund may experience delays and costs in recovering the securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability in the Statement of Net Assets for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Securities lending income represents fees charged to borrowers plus income earned on invested cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan. During the term of the loan, the fund is entitled to all distributions made on or in respect of the loaned securities.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>6. Credit Facility: The fund and certain other funds managed by The Vanguard Group (&#8220;Vanguard&#8221;) participate in a $3.1 billion committed credit facility provided by a syndicate of lenders pursuant to a credit agreement that may be renewed annually; each fund is individually liable for its borrowings, if any, under the credit facility. Borrowings may be utilized for temporary and emergency purposes, and are subject to the fund&#8217;s regulatory and contractual borrowing restrictions. The participating funds are charged administrative fees and an annual commitment fee of 0.10% of the undrawn amount of the facility; these fees are allocated to the funds based on a method approved by the fund&#8217;s board of trustees and included in Management and Administrative expenses on the fund&#8217;s Statement of Operations. Any borrowings under this facility bear interest at a rate based upon the higher of the one-month London Interbank Offered Rate, federal funds effective rate, or overnight bank funding rate plus an agreed-upon spread.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The fund had no borrowings outstanding at December 31, 2016, or at any time during the period then ended.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>7. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Premiums and discounts on debt securities purchased are amortized and accreted, respectively, to interest income over the lives of the respective securities. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial><STRONG>Value Index Fund</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=Arial><STRONG>Notes to Financial Statements</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Vanguard Value Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers four classes of shares: Investor Shares, ETF Shares, Admiral Shares, and Institutional Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#8217;s minimum purchase requirements. ETF Shares are listed for trading on NYSE Arca; they can be purchased and sold through a broker. Admiral Shares and Institutional Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, service, and account-size criteria.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>A. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. investment companies. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4 p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#8217;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#8217; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#8217;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market. Counterparty risk involving futures is mitigated because a regulated clearinghouse is the counterparty instead of the clearing broker. To further mitigate counterparty risk, the fund trades futures contracts on an exchange, monitors the financial strength of its clearing brokers and clearinghouse, and has entered into clearing agreements with its clearing brokers. The clearinghouse imposes initial margin requirements to secure the fund&#8217;s performance and requires daily settlement of variation margin representing changes in the market value of each contract.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate settlement values of the contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>During the year ended December 31, 2016, the fund&#8217;s average investments in long and short futures contracts represented less than 1% and 0% of net assets, respectively, based on the average of aggregate settlement values at each quarter-end during the period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>45</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<!--$$/page=--><A name="page_281"></A><BR>

<a name="_bclPageBorder281"></a><DIV style="PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial><STRONG>Value Index Fund</STRONG></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>3. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Management has analyzed the fund&#8217;s tax positions taken for all open federal income tax years (December 31, 2013&#8211;2016), and has concluded that no provision for federal income tax is required in the fund&#8217;s financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>4. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>5. Securities Lending: To earn additional income, the fund lends its securities to qualified institutional borrowers. Security loans are subject to termination by the fund at any time, and are required to be secured at all times by collateral in an amount at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. Daily market fluctuations could cause the value of loaned securities to be more or less than the value of the collateral received. When this occurs, the collateral is adjusted and settled on the next business day. The fund further mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into securities lending transactions only with a diverse group of prequalified counterparties, monitoring their financial strength, and entering into master securities lending agreements with its counterparties. The master securities lending agreements provide that, in the event of a counterparty&#8217;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may terminate any loans with that borrower, determine the net amount owed, and sell or retain the collateral up to the net amount owed to the fund; however, such actions may be subject to legal proceedings. While collateral mitigates counterparty risk, in the absence of a default the fund may experience delays and costs in recovering the securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability in the Statement of Net Assets for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Securities lending income represents fees charged to borrowers plus income earned on invested cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan. During the term of the loan, the fund is entitled to all distributions made on or in respect of the loaned securities.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>6. Credit Facility: The fund and certain other funds managed by The Vanguard Group (&#8220;Vanguard&#8221;) participate in a $3.1 billion committed credit facility provided by a syndicate of lenders pursuant to a credit agreement that may be renewed annually; each fund is individually liable for its borrowings, if any, under the credit facility. Borrowings may be utilized for temporary and emergency purposes, and are subject to the fund&#8217;s regulatory and contractual borrowing restrictions. The participating funds are charged administrative fees and an annual commitment fee of 0.10% of the undrawn amount of the facility; these fees are allocated to the funds based on a method approved by the fund&#8217;s board of trustees and included in Management and Administrative expenses on the fund&#8217;s Statement of Operations. Any borrowings under this facility bear interest at a rate based upon the higher of the one-month London Interbank Offered Rate, federal funds effective rate, or overnight bank funding rate plus an agreed-upon spread.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The fund had no borrowings outstanding at December 31, 2016, or at any time during the period then ended.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>7. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Premiums and discounts on debt securities purchased are amortized and accreted, respectively, to interest income over the lives of the respective securities. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Each class of shares has equal rights as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately bears certain class-specific expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in Management and Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses are allocated to each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees. Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>B. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>In accordance with the terms of a Funds&#8217; Service Agreement (the &#8220;FSA&#8221;) between Vanguard and the fund, Vanguard furnishes to the fund investment advisory, corporate management, administrative, marketing, and distribution services at Vanguard&#8217;s cost of operations (as defined by the FSA). These costs of operations are allocated to the fund based on methods and guidelines approved by the board of trustees. Vanguard does not require reimbursement in the current period for certain costs of operations (such as deferred compensation/benefits and risk/insurance costs); the fund&#8217;s liability for these costs of operations is included in Payables to Vanguard on the Statement of Net Assets.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Upon the request of Vanguard, the fund may invest up to 0.40% of its net assets as capital in Vanguard. At December 31, 2016, the fund had contributed to Vanguard capital in the amount of $3,668,000, representing 0.01% of the fund&#8217;s net assets and 1.47% of Vanguard&#8217;s capitalization. The fund&#8217;s trustees and officers are also directors and employees, respectively, of Vanguard.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>C. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Various inputs may be used to determine the value of the fund&#8217;s investments. <P style="MARGIN: 0px">&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Unrealized appreciation (depreciation) on open futures contracts is required to be treated as realized gain (loss) for tax purposes.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>E. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character. Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes. These differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as ordinary income for tax purposes.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>During the year ended December 31, 2016, the fund realized $1,144,327,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind redemptions&#8212;in which shareholders exchanged fund shares for securities held by the fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized losses to paid-in capital.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>For tax purposes, at December 31, 2016, the fund had $12,784,000 of ordinary income available for distribution. At December 31, 2016, the fund had available capital losses totaling $727,435,000 to offset future net capital gains. Of this amount, $333,377,000 is subject to expiration on December 31, 2017. Capital losses of $394,058,000 realized beginning in fiscal 2011 may be carried forward indefinitely under the Regulated Investment Company Modernization Act of 2010, but must be used before any expiring loss carryforwards.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>At December 31, 2016, the cost of investment securities for tax purposes was $40,669,088,000. Net unrealized appreciation of investment securities for tax purposes was $10,137,123,000, consisting of unrealized gains of $10,817,401,000 on securities that had risen in value since their purchase and $680,278,000 in unrealized losses on securities that had fallen in value since their purchase.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>F. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=Arial>During the year ended December 31, 2016, the fund purchased $13,254,049,000 of investment securities and sold $5,945,162,000 of investment securities, other than temporary cash investments. Purchases and sales include $8,173,611,000 and $3,074,773,000, respectively, in connection with in-kind purchases and redemptions of the fund&#8217;s capital shares.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Arial>The fund purchased securities from and sold securities to other Vanguard funds or accounts managed by Vanguard or its affiliates, in accordance with procedures adopted by the board of trustees in compliance with Rule 17a-7 of the Investment Company Act of 1940. For the year ended December 31, 2016, such purchases and sales were $961,457,000 and $750,250,000, respectively; these amounts are included in the purchases and sales of investment securities noted above.</FONT></P>
